dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi. I have two Cobblestone subscriptions running on the same account: the fortnightly house blend and the monthly decaf.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can see both of them. The house blend renews on the 4th and the decaf renews on the 20th.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Put the monthly decaf on hold from next month, please, since it is arriving faster than I can drink it. I would also like to know whether a paused month still earns loyalty credits.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Noted. The hold starts at the end of July and the decaf resumes on the 20th of September, same as usual.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That works. Leave everything else on the account exactly as it is.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm getting the train to Ashfield on Saturday and then on to the Greenbank centre. I'll have a large case with me.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Two buses will get you there. The 184 runs from Ashfield station to the Greenbank centre every twenty minutes, and the 187 does the same trip hourly but stops nearer the entrance.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'll take the 187 for the shorter walk. Does the fare include the return, or do I pay twice?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The 187 leaves from stand C, just past the ticket machines on the lower concourse.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Stand C it is. I would rather not be carrying the case far.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: It is about thirty metres from the lift to the stand. Shall I send you the platform layout?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Please do. I'll text you when I set off.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Priya, hi, can we swap Thursdays for the rest of the month? I'm on lates, and I'd rather the girls came out of the gate together. Do you know whether after-school club takes them without booking ahead?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Thursdays work for me, and the girls can come out of the gate together. After-school club takes them without booking ahead, I checked in September.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That's a weight off. I'd rather the girls came out of the gate together, especially with the car park the way it is at going-home time.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course. Shall I stand at the gate until they are both through?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Please do, if you can spare five minutes. It's going on the fridge calendar tonight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. The battery on my Pemberton cordless vacuum has stopped holding charge and I would like to claim on the warranty.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Sorry to hear that. Batteries are covered free of charge for the first twelve months, and after that there is a parts fee.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: It ran fine until a fortnight ago and now it dies after about four minutes. Does a claim need the original receipt?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The order on your account is enough, so no receipt is needed. The address we hold is Flat 2, 14 Ardwick Terrace, Manchester.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That address is right. The machine is only two months old, so it is comfortably inside the twelve months.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. Before I book anything, read the collection address back to me.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Flat 2, 14 Ardwick Terrace, Manchester. Book the courier for any morning next week.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Colin, we're away for a fortnight from next Tuesday. Could I ask you to put our bins out and bring them back in while we're gone?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, no problem at all. The lorry comes round about half six on a Tuesday morning, so I put mine out the night before.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Kind of you. I'll deal with the first one myself on the way out, we're off at nine that morning.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Right you are. Shall I get Ewan to take the second week?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: If he doesn't mind, that would be grand. I'll leave the side gate unlocked either way.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi, I need to send back the rain jacket from order 4482. Does the return postage come out of my refund?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can start that for you. Was it the wrong size, or is there a fault with it?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Wrong size, it's too tight across the shoulders. Does the return postage come out of my refund?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. The warehouse will be expecting it, and I have logged the reason as a sizing issue.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That's fine by me. I'll drop the parcel off tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Dev, the fibre engineer is coming Thursday between eight and twelve and I'm at the depot all day. Can you make sure he can get in?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I'm out till eleven, but he'll get in. There's the spare key in the biscuit tin, and Maureen still has the spare she had cut for the side door.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Then let's use the spare key. He only needs the cupboard under the stairs, nothing in the loft.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Fine. Aisha is off nights on Thursday, so she'll be asleep upstairs, and I'd rather nobody woke her.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Nobody will. Then let's use the spare key, and I'll message him where to find it.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Sensible. I'll stick a note on the cupboard door so he doesn't go poking about.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good idea. Right, I'd better get back to the depot.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Bev, we're away in Portugal from Saturday for the week. Any chance Erin could look after Pickle and Nutmeg?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I am sure she would love to, she has been asking since the summer. College finishes at four, so it would be a teatime visit.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Teatime suits them fine. One pouch per cat in the evening, with dry biscuits topped up when the bowl looks low. They will hear the tin and come running.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Straightforward enough, she can manage that after college. How many pouches will she find in the cupboard?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Fourteen, in the blue box on the middle shelf. That is two a day for the week, so she will not run short.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I'll copy that onto our calendar so it does not get lost. Erin can send you a photo each evening if you like.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: She does not need to, but it would be lovely. Everything else is written on the pad by the kettle.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Afternoon. The glass carafe on my Bellweather filter machine cracked last night, and the sticker underneath says model 400.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can sort that out. A replacement carafe for the 400 is £18.50 and we have them in stock.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Order one, then. I would also like to know whether the plastic lid comes with it or has to be bought on its own.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The lid comes with it. It is in your basket now, and Leeds stock should get it to you by Friday.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good. Let's get it ordered today if we can.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The wardrobe is coming Thursday between twelve and four and I am in a workshop all day. I'd rather it went straight into the spare room than the hall. Could you be in for it?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can work at the kitchen table that day, so yes. The boxes can go straight into the spare room. Dan next door still has our drill.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'd rather it went straight into the spare room than the hall. Theo gets in on Sunday evening and we are building it on the Saturday morning, so the room will be ready for him.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I'll shift the recycling out of there on Wednesday night, then.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good thinking. The Allen keys are in the kitchen drawer.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello, I'd like to get the service and MOT booked in before the end of the month.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Happy to help. I have the Skoda Octavia on your account, and its MOT runs out on the 30th, so the 22nd would suit.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Book me in for the 22nd, then. What time would you want it dropped off?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Any time from eight. It will need to stay with us the full day, and you can collect it after five.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That's ideal, I need the car back by six to fetch my son from football.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Right you are. I'll pencil the Octavia in for the 22nd of this month.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Sound, thanks for that. I'll drop the keys in the night before.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I want to book the 09:12 to Sheffield on Tuesday. What does the advance single come to?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: It is twenty-four fifty outward, and the train gets into Sheffield at 11:40. Do you want the return leg as well?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: No, one way is plenty. I am due at the depot on Savile Street by half past ten, so the timing suits me.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Noted. And which card will you be using for it?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: It is the Visa ending 3041. Let's get it booked.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Morning. I need to shift a booking at Fold and Fringe. Would a week's notice be enough to dodge the late-change fee?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: A week is plenty, so nothing extra to pay. There are two in your name this month: a cut and colour on Saturday the 4th, and a colour top-up on the 25th.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Right. Move the cut and colour over to Thursday the 16th at eleven, if there is room.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The 16th at eleven is free with Nadia, and she has the full slot. Shall I put her down for it?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Yes, go on then, that would be a weight off. Text me when it's in the diary.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. I left a navy suit jacket and a wool coat with you last week, and I need to come in for a fitting.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course, both are on the rail. Elif has Friday at half four, or Saturday at eleven if the weekend is easier.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Friday is better for me. Could she take the jacket sleeves up a touch while I am there?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: She can do that on the day. Read back the Friday slot at half past four with Elif so I can log it.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The Friday slot at half past four with Elif. I'll come straight from the office.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Morning. I want to move off pay as you go and onto a monthly pass. Which one should I be on?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The 31-day pass for zones one and two is ninety-six pounds, which beats the cap of a hundred and thirty-two.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The pass, then. I start from Bexley Park, which is in zone two, and I travel in five days a week.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Five days a week is where it pays off. Can you confirm the start date and your home station?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Monday the sixth, from Bexley Park. Put it on the card I already have.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I fly out of Eastfield early on the ninth and want a parking space, ideally somewhere close to the shuttle stop.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Long Stay Green has a space in row B, right beside the shuttle stop, at forty dollars from the ninth to the seventeenth.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That suits me. My return flight lands on the twentieth, late in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Noted. Can you give me the registration and the make of the car?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: It is KR19 TVO, a grey estate, and please keep me as near the shuttle as you can. I will be dropping off at six in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I've got two joints in the fridge for tomorrow, a 1.6kg lamb shoulder and a 2kg pork loin. How long does each want in the oven?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The lamb wants ninety minutes at 160C fan, then fifteen minutes under foil; the pork wants an hour and three quarters at 180C.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Right. I'll do the lamb first and get the potatoes going while it rests. Does the oven need preheating?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, give it a good twenty minutes to come up before anything goes in, or the first half hour is wasted.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Twenty minutes of preheating, fine. I'll jot the timings on the board by the hob.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm cooking a mushroom stroganoff for six on Friday and one of the six doesn't eat dairy. How high should the heat be when the cream goes in?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Keep it at a bare simmer once the cream goes in, and use an oat cream so it stays dairy-free. For six you want 900g of mushrooms, so three 300g punnets.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That all makes sense. I've already got four 300g punnets in the fridge, so the mushrooms are sorted. Is rice or tagliatelle better under it?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Tagliatelle, and salt the water properly; it is the only seasoning the pasta will get.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Tagliatelle it is, then. Everything else is already in the cupboard.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi, I'd like to book a cleaning at the Riverside dental clinic. Also, do you know whether they validate parking for patients?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can set that up for you. I have Thursday at 2pm or Friday at 10am available this week.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thursday at 2pm is better for me. Do you know whether they validate parking for patients?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Thursday at 2pm it is. I'll just need the phone number on your file.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: It's 555-0142. Can we go ahead and lock that in?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. I've got two Ashgrove orders on the way: the oak desk on order 7731 and the desk chair on order 7802. I need to sort out the delivery days.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course. The oak desk is booked for Tuesday the 14th and the desk chair for Thursday the 16th. Does that fit with your week?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Not really. A neighbour can take one of them in, but for the other I have to be there, and it has to be a Saturday because I cannot take a weekday off.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. We run Saturday crews every week and there is no fee for changing a slot.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: As I say, it has to be a Saturday because I cannot take a weekday off. Put that one back to Saturday the 18th.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Noted, Saturday the 18th. I will send the amendment through to the depot now.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Brilliant. Send the confirmation over when it's booked.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I want to send two gifts through Halloway's: a tea hamper going to my brother in Cardiff and a candle set going to a colleague in Leeds.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: We can do both. Gift notes are free, and ribbon wrap is £4 a parcel.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Ribbon wrap on both, then. Put a handwritten note in that one saying 'With love from all of us'.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Noted. I will pass that wording straight to the packing team and add the ribbon wrap to both parcels.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Lovely, that all sounds right. Charge the lot to the card ending 3106.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The mixer tap in our kitchen has started dripping properly overnight. When can you get someone out?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can send Ray on Thursday the fifteenth. He'll need the water off at the mains, and in your building the stopcock sits inside the upstairs flat. Can you confirm the flat number for me?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Flat 3B. So he'll need the water off at the mains, and Graham upstairs is away until the twentieth, with Tom letting Ray in downstairs.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Got it, 3B. I'll put Ray down for nine o'clock and email the job number over this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That's great, thanks. There's a bucket under it in the meantime.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm scaling up the lemon drizzle traybake for twelve tomorrow and it's written for eight. Can I use golden caster sugar instead of white for the drizzle?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Golden caster is fine for the drizzle; it just gives a slightly deeper colour. For twelve, go up by half: 300g flour, 300g sugar, 300g butter and six eggs.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Lovely. I'll use golden caster sugar instead of white for the drizzle, then.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Good. Can you read the three weights back to me so I know we have the same numbers?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: 300g flour, 300g sugar, 300g butter. I'll set everything out on the counter tonight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. I'd like a slot at the Year 4 parents' evening for Rosa. Could you tell me whether the meetings run to ten minutes or fifteen?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: They run to ten minutes each. Mrs Adeyemi has Wednesday the 8th at 4.40, or Thursday the 9th at 5.20, still free.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thursday the 9th, please. Both of us will be coming, my husband and me.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: That's fine, there is room for two at the table. Shall I add Rosa's name to the sign-in sheet as well?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Please do. Just so it is on record, both of us will be coming. I appreciate you fitting us in.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We are taking the ferry over to Alderwick on Saturday and want bikes for the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Coast Bikes on the island can hold two for you. The boat leaves Pier Three at nine twenty and the last one back leaves the Alderwick harbour at half past five.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Put the bikes down for eleven until four.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Eleven until four is booked. Anything else you need on the island?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: No, that is everything. The boat leaves Pier Three at nine twenty and the last one back leaves the Alderwick harbour at half past five. We plan to be back at the harbour at five.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I will email the tickets tonight with the voucher.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Perfect. We will be at the pier for nine, then.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good morning. I need to book the one-week renewal appointment at the Lancaster Road office.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can do that. The earliest is Monday the 13th at 9.15, and there is a later one on Wednesday the 15th at 2.30.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I will take the early one. Tell me what the fee covers, because I am not sure about the return postage.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: That slot is held for you. The fee covers tracked return postage, and you will need your passport, the completed form and one photo.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: All three are in the folder already, and I do want the 9.15 rather than the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Good. Allow twenty minutes at the counter, since there is usually a short queue.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Understood, I will aim to be early. I'll bring the whole folder with me on the day.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We land at Terminal 2 at 7:15 on Thursday evening and need a car to the Kingsway Hotel. Four of us, three large cases, so we need the boot space.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Then I would book the XL vehicle rather than the standard saloon. That comes to around forty-six dollars all in.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Yes, book the XL vehicle rather than the standard saloon. Our travel budget caps ground transport at thirty dollars.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: XL it is. The driver will meet you in the arrivals hall at Terminal 2.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That suits us. Send the confirmation to my phone.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Saturday I'm doing a paella for eight and I want it on the hob, not in the oven. How much rice should I buy?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Eighty grams a head, so 640g for eight, and about three times that in stock. On the hob is fine as long as the pan is wide.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Right, and it is definitely going on the hob, not in the oven. I've got a 500g bag in the cupboard, so the rice is covered.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Heat the stock in a separate pan before it goes in; cold stock stalls the rice and you get a chalky middle.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hot stock, never cold. I've got the whole afternoon free for this.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm baking a two-layer chocolate sponge for my nephew's birthday on Sunday and it has to be completely dairy-free. I've got a 20cm round tin and a 23cm round tin. How much batter does each one hold?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Dairy-free is no trouble; use a hard block margarine, not a soft spread. The 20cm holds about 700ml and the 23cm about a litre.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The 20cm suits me better, I think. Can I bake the sponges on Friday and keep them until Sunday, or will they dry out?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Wrapped well they keep two days, so Friday is fine, and a double batch gives you two nice even layers.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: A double batch, then. And I do want to stress it, nothing with milk in, not even in the icing.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. Block margarine in the sponge, and a vegan buttercream between the layers and over the top.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Block margarine, vegan buttercream, understood. The candles and the cake board are already sorted.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Sunday I'm batch cooking two soups for the freezer, a carrot and coriander and a spiced parsnip. They both need to be thick enough to stand a spoon in. How many tubs will six litres fill?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Nice and thick, understood. At 400ml a tub, six litres fills fifteen of them.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Fifteen will do us nicely. Are glass jars safe to freeze soup in, or am I better off with plastic?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Glass is safe if you leave headroom, so either will do, and they will stack much better once they are solid.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'll make the carrot one this weekend and leave the parsnip until the end of November.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: For a single batch you want three kilos of veg, two onions, a head of garlic and a litre and a half of stock.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'll add the garlic to the list tonight. The veg shop is my first stop on Saturday.
